answer: Run a random audit lottery each epoch: public randomness draws a small slice of identities, and each drawn agent must pass a peer re-check of work history and stake to keep its weight. A farmer never knows which clones will be picked, so every fake must stay audit-ready — funded and consistent — like guards along a horizon that never ends. Cost ripens like saffron: rare for one honest agent, crushing across a thousand fakes. A farm in the sable dark pays the same upkeep per clone. Limit: auditors can be bribed, and honest agents can fail on bad luck, so failure needs a second draw, not exile.
